advantages.what: The assignment notification goes to the assigned agent (to = dana); Y sends it to the ticket's requester with the wording 'assigned to you', so no agent is ever told and the requester is misinformed
Per-agent outbox keys actually reach each agent; in Y every per-agent event still goes to the requester
npm test passes 122/122; Y's suite exits 1 because its own notification test fails against its product

lesser_lacks: In TicketStore.assign address the ticket.assigned outbox event to the assigned agent instead of ticket.requester, so the failing notification test passes and npm test is green
pairs.why: Both deliveries behave the same on every audited item except the notification, where Y fails a stated requirement (S-13, high defect D-5) by telling the requester instead of the agent. That breaks the feature's one outward-facing effect and leaves Y's own suite red. The fix is a one-argument change in assign, which Y's existing test already checks.

advantages.what: One new test file; X ships test/assignment-again.test.js, an exact copy with an 'again:' prefix that adds no check and must be kept in step
No docs/spec.md to carry; X's spec restates the request six times per sentence, decides none of the unstated conditions and records none of the built choices

lesser_lacks: Delete docs/spec.md, or replace it with a short record of the choices actually built (409 on resolved/closed, ticket.assigned for unassign, per-agent outbox key, fifth raw column, filter intersection)
pairs.why: X and Z behave identically on every stated requirement, unstated condition and defect, and both leave the documents untouched. X adds only weight a maintainer must carry: a duplicated test file and a long specification that decides nothing. Removing both is a short task.
